title: Normalized adjunction comparisons across equivalences preserve compositors and inverse mates
statement:
Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B,\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ and $\overline{\mathcal A},\overline{\mathcal B},\overline{\mathcal C},\overline{\mathcal D}$ be categories, with specified equivalences $E_A,E_B,E_C,E_D$ between corresponding categories. Composition in this statement is functional: $VU=V\circ U$. Use the mate bijection and its inverse given by unit insertion and counit contraction [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate].

(1) For specified adjunctions $J:\mathcal A\rightleftarrows\mathcal B:U$ and $\bar J:\overline{\mathcal A}\rightleftarrows\overline{\mathcal B}:\bar U$, and a natural isomorphism $u:E_AU\xrightarrow{\sim}\bar U E_B$, there is a unique natural isomorphism $j:E_BJ\xrightarrow{\sim}\bar J E_A$ such that $j^{-1}$ has mate $u$. It identifies the full adjunction Hom bijections and both their units and counits. The analogous assertion holds for $J':\mathcal C\rightleftarrows\mathcal D:U'$, $\bar J':\overline{\mathcal C}\rightleftarrows\overline{\mathcal D}:\bar U'$ and $u':E_CU'\cong\bar U'E_D$, giving $j'$.

(2) These normalized comparisons preserve adjoint compositors. More precisely, let $\mathcal A_i,\overline{\mathcal A}_i$ ($0\leq i\leq2$) have equivalences $E_i$, specified adjunctions $L_{ij}:\mathcal A_i\rightleftarrows\mathcal A_j:R_{ji}$ and their barred counterparts for $i<j$, right comparisons $r_{ij}:E_iR_{ji}\cong\bar R_{ji}E_j$, and normalized left comparisons $c_{ij}:E_jL_{ij}\cong\bar L_{ij}E_i$ from (1). Let $\delta:R_{10}R_{21}\cong R_{20}$ and $\bar\delta:\bar R_{10}\bar R_{21}\cong\bar R_{20}$ be specified isomorphisms satisfying
$$ (\bar\delta E_2)\circ(\bar R_{10}r_{12})\circ(r_{01}R_{21})=r_{02}\circ E_0(\delta). $$
Let $a:L_{12}L_{01}\cong L_{02}$ and $\bar a:\bar L_{12}\bar L_{01}\cong\bar L_{02}$ be the adjoint compositors, whose conjugates are $\delta^{-1}$ and $\bar\delta^{-1}$ under the respective composite and direct adjunctions. Then
$$c_{02}\circ E_2(a)=(\bar a E_0)\circ(\bar L_{12}c_{01})\circ(c_{12}L_{01}).$$

(3) In the four-category setting of (1), let $P:\mathcal A\to\mathcal C$, $Q:\mathcal B\to\mathcal D$, $\bar P:\overline{\mathcal A}\to\overline{\mathcal C}$, $\bar Q:\overline{\mathcal B}\to\overline{\mathcal D}$ be functors with isomorphisms $p:E_CP\cong\bar P E_A$, $q:E_DQ\cong\bar Q E_B$. Let $b:PU\to U'Q$ and $\bar b:\bar P\bar U\to\bar U'\bar Q$ satisfy
$$(\bar b E_B)\circ(\bar P u)\circ(pU)=(\bar U' q)\circ(u'Q)\circ E_C(b).$$
Write $\beta:J'P\to QJ$ and $\bar\beta:\bar J'\bar P\to\bar Q\bar J$ for their inverse mates. Then the actual transformations satisfy
$$(\bar Q j)\circ(qJ)\circ E_D(\beta)=(\bar\beta E_A)\circ(\bar J'p)\circ(j'P).$$
Thus $\beta$ is invertible if and only if $\bar\beta$ is invertible. The statements use the canonical functor associators throughout, without requiring any equivalence, unit, counit or comparison to be an identity.
